#### Total Fiber Capacity Over Time

• Early 2010s Commercial systems reached about 10 Tbps per fiber using the C-band 
• Mid-2010s to 2020 C+L band systems became available, allowing to double fiber capacity 
• 2021–2023 Fiber Spectral Efficiency very close to Shannon limit thanks to Next Generation Coherent WDM interfaces 

#### Is it Convenient to Continue to Widen the Bands?

• Widening the optical spectrum leads to increased amplifier noise and higher average ripple, both of which can reduce system performance and require more pumps and higher power to compensate 
• Noise levels rise at the far end of the spectrum, requiring WDM Interfaces to operate at lower data rates and decreasing usable capacity in the L-band 
• Shifting the L-band or using a Super L-band (6THz) further increases noise and ripple, leading to degraded overall network performance. EDFA technology not ready for deployment to cover 1620nm region 

#### Cisco NCS 1010 Open Line System

• Universal Form Factor • 3RU, 19” wide, 300mm deep Box • Simple Pre-configured Chassis • ROADM Degree / Terminal • Optical Line Amplifier

• Flexible Platform • C-band only or C&L-band • EDFA only or EDFA+Raman • Defined with Automation in mind

#### The Perfect Balance between Integration & Separation

• Integrated Line Cards • Better MTBF, fewer Field errors • Cookie Cutter Approach • One Line Card per Shelf and one Shelf variant for All sites

• Dedicated C-Band & L-Band Shelves

• Defer cost of L-Band day-1 
• Bands operate mostly independent of each other - better reliability. 

• NTA upgrade from C-band to C&L-band

First Pluggable to Break into the Terabit Era!

• Co-packaging of DSP and SiPh optics (OE-MCM – like 400ZR)

• Size, Power, Reliability and Performances advantages
